insights.headline: Gold and silver extend Friday rebound as Wall Street rallies; Fed hike bets still cap gains
insights.summary: Gold climbed above $3,650 and silver surged past $43.60 late on Friday as a tech-led Wall Street rally and renewed Chinese physical demand extended the rebound from Wednesday's 15-month lows. MCX gold held near Rs 1,26,251 per 10 g with silver near Rs 1,54,804 per kg, while COMEX gold settled 4% higher at $3,708. The rally still faces a December Fed hike that markets have nearly fully priced, with the US jobs report on Dec 4 the next test.
points: Spot gold rose 2.45% to $3,653 late Friday and silver jumped 5.32% to $43.62 as Wall Street posted its best week since April 2025.
MCX gold rebounded Rs 8,345 from Wednesday's low to Rs 1,26,251 per 10 g, set to snap a two-week losing streak; MCX silver hit Rs 1,54,804 per kg.
India's silver imports nearly tripled in October to Rs 18,634 crore as import rules eased, with silver ETF inflows of Rs 3,092 crore.
Gold ETFs saw $2.15 billion of net outflows last week as higher rates drew money away from bullion, World Gold Council data shows.
Kitco's survey: 40% of Wall Street analysts see gold higher next week after the $3,600 reclaim; Main Street stayed bearish, with payrolls the next test.

brief.headline: Gold, silver extend Friday rebound as Wall Street rallies
brief.summary: MCX gold held near Rs 1,26,251 per 10 g and silver near Rs 1,54,804 per kg after spot gold rose to $3,653 on Friday.

bullets.text: Steadier tech stocks and a softer dollar drove the rebound from Wednesday's 15-month lows, Mint says, with Beijing's support adding lift.
MCX gold is set to snap a two-week losing streak as wedding demand returns, Mint reports; silver imports nearly tripled in October.
Watch next week: Chicago PMI on Monday and the US jobs report on Friday, the next test for the rebound, Kitco's survey notes.

trending.title: The rebound, and what caps it
trending.summary: Gold and silver bounced off 15-month lows on bargain buying and a Wall Street rally, but a December Fed hike is nearly fully priced, so rallies toward $3,750 could draw sellers.

trending.title: India's silver buyers are back
trending.summary: October silver imports nearly tripled to Rs 18,634 crore after import rules eased, and silver ETF inflows hit Rs 3,092 crore. November trade data, due Dec 15, will show whether the buying lasts.

trending.title: China lifts the mood
trending.summary: Beijing's pledge to support its stock market sent the CSI300 up 4.2%, and Chinese physical demand helped gold and silver seal their first weekly gains in three.

trending.title: ETF money leaves while physical buyers return
trending.summary: Gold ETFs bled $2.15 billion last week on rate worries, while Indian and Chinese physical demand revived at lower prices.

trending.title: RBI brings its gold home
trending.summary: RBI moved 60 tonnes of gold from overseas vaults to India in April–September, taking domestic holdings to 84% of its 880.52-tonne reserves; forex reserves slipped to a 16-week low of $700.90 billion.

items.title: MCX gold prices rebound over ₹8,300 in two sessions, set to snap 2-week losing streak; what lifted sentiment?
items.summary: MCX gold rose nearly Rs 4,000 per 10 g on Friday to an intraday high of Rs 1,26,251, Mint reports, rebounding Rs 8,345 from Wednesday's low and set to snap a two-week losing streak as steadier tech stocks and a softer dollar lifted sentiment; MCX silver surged Rs 9,000 per kg to Rs 1,54,804.

items.title: Gold climbs above $3,650, silver surges as Wall Street rebounds sharply - Kitco PM Report
items.summary: Spot gold climbed above $3,650 late on Friday, up 2.45% at $3,653, while silver surged 5.32% to $43.62, Kitco reports, as a tech-led Wall Street rally and renewed Chinese physical demand extended the rebound from Wednesday's 15-month lows. Gold traded between $3,569.60 and $3,686; traders now watch Monday's Chicago PMI and Friday's US jobs report.

items.title: COMEX Gold Surges 4% to $3,708, MCX Gold Crosses ₹1.26 Lakh; COMEX Silver Futures Jumps 10%
items.summary: COMEX gold futures jumped 4% to $3,708.40 on Friday, extending the rebound from a 52-week low, while MCX gold rose 3.2% to an intraday high of ₹1,26,251 per 10 g. COMEX silver futures surged over 10% to $44.24 an ounce as risk appetite returned across Asian markets and Chinese stocks rallied.

items.title: Silver Imports Surge in India as Buyers Return, October Data Shows
items.summary: India's silver imports nearly tripled in October to Rs 18,634 crore after import rules eased, FXEmpire reports, with silver ETF inflows of Rs 3,092 crore, up 57% on September. The author estimates imports of roughly 32 to 36 million ounces, while China exported 285.43 tonnes as its own demand stayed strong.

items.title: India Now Stores 84% of Its Gold Reserves Domestically: RBI Brings Back 60 Tonnes From Overseas Vaults
items.summary: RBI's half-yearly report shows it moved 60.08 tonnes of gold from overseas vaults to India between April and September, taking domestic holdings to 740.13 tonnes — 84% of its 880.52-tonne total — without adding to overall reserves.

items.title: Gold, Silver Prices Rebound as Bullion Recovers From Lows
items.summary: Gold and silver ended a volatile week with a sharp Friday rebound: spot gold rose 3% to $3,672 and silver 6.6% to $44.28, recovering from Wednesday's 15-month low of $3,426 after hot October core PCE (3.3%) lifted Fed hike bets. MCX December silver futures jumped 5.1% to ₹1,53,277 per kg as steadier tech stocks and bargain buying drove the recovery.

items.title: Gold and Silver Jump as Beijing Vows to Support China's Stock Market
items.summary: Gold and silver jumped on Friday after Beijing promised support for China's stock market, BullionVault reports, with London gold peaking at $3,685 and silver trading 15.1% above Wednesday's 15-month lows. Shanghai's CSI300 leapt 4.2% as the State Council urged listed firms to raise dividends and buybacks with ample liquidity guarantees. Both metals sealed their first weekly gains in three.

items.title: Gold and Silver Price Forecast: Silver Leads Rebound as Ratio Falls
items.summary: FXEmpire's technical read has gold testing $3,700 resistance after rebounding from the $3,400-$3,500 support zone, with a break above opening the $3,900-$4,000 zone; silver needs to clear $49 to extend toward $58, and the gold-to-silver ratio falling from 89.70 suggests silver is leading the recovery - though high rates may still cap gains.

items.title: Gold rebounds from one-year low as AI jitters ease
items.summary: Spot gold rose 1.6% to $3,622.91 on Friday, rebounding from its lowest since September 2025 as a US holiday lull calmed AI-driven market jitters, Reuters reports; bullion is up 2.7% on the week, silver climbed 4.6% to $43.40, and China's net gold imports via Hong Kong hit their highest since April.

items.title: Gold's $3,750 ceiling: Analyst says a hawkish Fed "would cap Gold rallies"
items.summary: Gold is back above $3,600 and heading for a weekly gain after bouncing from a 15-month low near $3,425, FXStreet reports, but analysts say a hawkish Fed would cap rallies below $3,750; $3,500 must hold for the recovery to last, with the Fed's Dec 8-9 meeting the key test.

items.title: Wall Street's bullish bets tick higher after gold bounces back above $3,600, Main Street maintains bearish bias with payrolls on deck
items.summary: Wall Street turned less bearish after gold reclaimed $3,600, Kitco's weekly survey shows: 6 of 15 analysts (40%) expect higher prices next week and 5 (33%) expect a fall. Main Street stayed bearish, with 43% of 159 retail voters looking for lower prices. Analysts pointed to the rebound from Wednesday's $3,426 low, with Friday's US jobs report the next test.

items.title: HSBC flags $3,400 as gold's next big test and says it is too early to call a bottom
items.summary: HSBC warns it is too early to call an end to gold's slide, InvestingLive reports, with further equity weakness able to push gold through major support at $3,400 an ounce; the bank sees limits to the selloff, while Saxo's Ole Hansen says gold's slide from its record looks overdone.

items.title: Gold's $2.15 Billion ETF Exodus Highlights the Cost of Higher Rates
items.summary: Gold ETFs recorded net outflows of $2.15 billion last week, World Gold Council data shows, as higher interest rates raised the cost of holding non-yielding bullion, with investors rotating toward yield-bearing assets.

items.title: Gold Remains Under Pressure as the Weekly Close Fails to Reclaim $3,618
items.summary: Gold remained under pressure into the weekend, Investing.com's weekly review says, with the weekly close failing to retake a key level even after Friday's rebound from 15-month lows. The review reads the bounce as unconfirmed while Fed hike bets keep a lid on rallies.

items.title: India's forex reserves fall $4.44 billion to $700.90 billion, says RBI
items.summary: India's forex reserves fell $4.44 billion to $700.90 billion in the week ended November 20, RBI data shows, with gold reserves down $4.10 billion to $94.52 billion as lower bullion prices cut their value; foreign currency assets eased $266 million to $583.19 billion.

items.title: Sebi allows FPIs to trade in physically settled non-agri commodity derivatives
items.summary: SEBI will allow foreign portfolio investors to trade physically settled non-agricultural commodity derivatives from June 2027, Mint reports, revising a framework that restricted FPI participation to cash-settled non-agri contracts and indices.

items.title: Spot gold up as futures rebound from 1-year low; wedding demand lends support
items.summary: Spot gold in India rose on Friday as MCX December gold touched ₹1,25,912 per 10 g, up 3%, and COMEX gold reached $3,683, with wedding-season demand and recycled-gold buying supporting prices. Informist notes jewellers offered no discounts as demand rose, though traders expect Fed hike bets to limit further gains.

items.title: Gold demand revives in India, China as price slide sparks bargain buying
items.summary: Gold demand in India and China revived this week as prices fell to their lowest in over a year, BusinessLine reports, with Indian domestic gold near ₹124,800 per 10 g after touching ₹1,17,906 and dealer premiums up to $19 an ounce as jewellers restock for the wedding season; China's net gold imports via Hong Kong hit their highest since April.

items.title: MCX market cap hits ₹1 trillion; stock rallies 11% in two days, up 77% YTD
items.summary: MCX shares hit a new high of ₹3,939.85 on Friday, taking the exchange's market value past ₹1 trillion, Business Standard reports; the stock is up 11% in two days and 77% so far this year, more than doubling from its 52-week low.

items.title: Titan, TBZ: Jewellery, gold financiers' stocks rise as bullion rebounds 2%
items.summary: Jewellery stocks rallied as bullion rebounded, Business Standard reports: Titan rose 3.7% to ₹4,805, Kalyan Jewellers gained 3.8% and PC Jeweller added 2%, tracking MCX gold's recovery to ₹1,24,787 per 10 g.

items.title: Rupee rally faces oil test; inflows, positive sentiment provide cushion
items.summary: The rupee's November rally, up 2.6% this month and Asia's best, faces a test from Brent crude above $96, though $16 billion of foreign equity inflows in November and improving sentiment towards Indian assets should cushion it, Reuters reports. The currency settled at 92.4450 to the dollar on Thursday, with the dollar index near a 22-month high.

items.title: Gold Prices Fall: Is India’s ₹23 Lakh Crore Gold Loan Market at Risk? | The Morning Brief Decode
items.summary: ET’s Morning Brief looks at the strain on India’s ₹23 lakh crore gold-loan market after gold’s sharp fall from its peak, with rising loan-to-value ratios squeezing borrowers and lenders. It examines whether lenders can auction pledged jewellery even without a missed repayment, why the RBI is concerned about repeat borrowers, and how exposed India’s biggest gold-loan companies are.

items.title: Turkish central bank suspends its purchases of domestically produced gold, bankers say
items.summary: Turkey's central bank has suspended purchases of domestically produced gold until further notice, bankers told Reuters, without giving a reason. Turkey mines about 30 tonnes a year and the bank holds around 800 tonnes. The pause breaks a run of central-bank buying that has long supported gold.
